questions.question: A team wants raw virtual machines in AWS where they control the operating system and installed software, without managing physical hardware. Which AWS service provides this Infrastructure as a Service capability?
options: Amazon EC2
Amazon EBS
Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
AWS Auto Scaling Group
questions.explanation: EC2 is AWS's IaaS offering that rents virtual machines in the cloud. EBS provides network-attached virtual drives for data, not compute. ELB distributes traffic across machines rather than providing them. An Auto Scaling Group adjusts the number of instances but is not itself the rented VM service.
questions.keyTopic: EC2 as Infrastructure as a Service

questions.question: A solutions architect is describing what EC2 as an offering covers to a colleague who thinks it is only virtual machines. Which set of capabilities correctly matches each capability to its role?
options: EC2 rents VMs, EBS stores data on virtual drives, ELB distributes load, ASG scales instances automatically
EC2 rents VMs, EBS distributes load, ELB stores data on virtual drives, ASG restricts traffic
EC2 stores data on virtual drives, EBS rents VMs, ELB scales instances, ASG distributes load
EC2 rents VMs, EBS scales instances, ELB stores data on drives, ASG distributes load
questions.explanation: The source maps each capability: EC2 rents virtual machines, EBS stores data on virtual drives, ELB distributes load across machines, and ASG scales services automatically. The other options swap these roles (EBS for load balancing, ELB for storage, ASG for distribution or storage), which misrepresents each service.
questions.keyTopic: Renting VMs, EBS, ELB, ASG roles

questions.question: A company needs web traffic spread across several EC2 instances and the fleet size to grow and shrink with demand, with no manual intervention. Which combination of capabilities matches these two requirements?
options: Elastic Load Balancing to distribute traffic and an Auto Scaling Group to scale instances
An Auto Scaling Group to distribute traffic and EBS to scale instances
EBS to distribute traffic and Elastic Load Balancing to scale instances
EC2 Instance Store to distribute traffic and a security group to scale instances
questions.explanation: ELB is the capability for distributing load across machines, and ASG scales services automatically by adding or removing instances. The other options assign distribution and scaling to EBS, Instance Store or security groups, which are storage and firewall features, not load distribution or scaling.
questions.keyTopic: Renting VMs, EBS, ELB, ASG roles

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the EC2 sizing and configuration choices made at launch?
options: The number of Availability Zones the instance will replicate across
The operating system, such as Linux, Windows or Mac OS
The amount of compute power and number of CPU cores
The network card speed and whether the instance has a public IP address
questions.explanation: Launch-time options listed are OS, CPU power and cores, RAM, storage type and space, network card (speed, public IP), firewall rules (security group) and User Data. Replication across Availability Zones is an architecture decision beyond per-instance sizing options, so it is not a launch configuration choice. The other three options are all explicitly launch-time choices.

questions.question: An architect is choosing launch settings for a new instance and wants the firewall rules that permit or block traffic defined as part of that instance's configuration. Which launch option provides this?
options: A security group
An EC2 User Data script
An EBS volume
The instance's public IP address setting
questions.explanation: The security group is the set of firewall rules for the instance and is one of the sizing/configuration options set at launch. User Data is a bootstrap script, not traffic control. EBS is network-attached storage, not a firewall. A public IP setting affects addressing and reachability, not which traffic is permitted or denied.
questions.keyTopic: Security group as firewall rule set

questions.question: An instance must have security patches and a web server package installed the first time it boots, without anyone logging in. What should the architect configure?
options: An EC2 User Data bootstrap script that runs commands at first start
An EBS volume pre-loaded with the software, attached after launch
Manual configuration after the instance is running, performed each reboot
An Auto Scaling Group that installs packages when it adds instances
questions.explanation: User Data is a bootstrap script that launches commands automatically when the instance first starts, ideal for installing updates and software. EBS stores data but does not run install commands by itself. Manual post-launch configuration requires logging in, which the requirement forbids. An ASG manages instance count and does not itself install packages.

questions.question: A team reports that software installed by the User Data script was present after the first boot, but the script did not re-run when the instance was later stopped and started again. What explains this behavior?
options: User Data runs only once, at the instance's first start
User Data runs on every start unless the instance is rebooted
User Data only runs when the instance is terminated and replaced
User Data runs only after an operator logs in as root
questions.explanation: The User Data script is executed only once, at the instance's first start, so later starts do not repeat it. It does not run on every start (or be skipped only on reboot), it is not tied to termination, and it executes at first boot rather than waiting for an interactive root login.
questions.keyTopic: User Data runs once as root

questions.question: A User Data script must install system packages during the instance's first boot. Which statement about how the script executes is correct?
options: It runs with the root user, so it has full privileges on the instance
It runs as an unprivileged user and needs sudo configured for privileged tasks
It runs with the same permissions as the IAM user who launched the instance
It runs as a temporary user that is deleted once bootstrapping finishes
questions.explanation: The source states the User Data script runs with the root user, giving full privileges for privileged boot tasks. It is not run as an unprivileged or temporary user, and its privileges are not tied to the launching IAM user's identity.
questions.keyTopic: User Data runs once as root

questions.question: A workload needs a disk physically attached to the instance's own host hardware, rather than a drive reached over the network. Which storage choice fits?
options: EC2 Instance Store
Amazon EBS
Amazon EFS
An EBS volume mounted with a public IP address
questions.explanation: Instance Store is the hardware storage option physically attached to the host machine. EBS and EFS are both network-attached storage reached over the network, not host hardware. Attaching a public IP to an EBS volume does not change its network-attached nature.
